result.summary:
ISSUE-FIXER, WF-03 steps 0.5 and 1 for ISS-0002. Diagnosis only: no code or docs changed; every run used scratch copies. Next: route to CODE-DESIGNER for the fix design (WF-03 step 2).

IN SHORT. Not a recurrence. Reproduced, and the defect is wider than the issue says. The write phase of apply-verdict (tools/src/apply.js:100-107) writes up to three files in place, one after another, STATE.md first. Nothing is staged, pre-checked, rolled back or caught. There are two mechanisms. M1 (the issue's case): a later file fails, so the earlier ones stay written. M2 (not in the issue): an in-place write fails part-way and leaves its own target truncated, STATE.md included. M2 emptied STATE.md, owner's section and all, and after that the tool refuses to re-run. Design §5 promises "no write on error" but treats the write phase as infallible, and §6 has no code for it. The tests exercise only the validation half of §5.

STEP 0.5 - REGISTRY LOOKUP: no prior match.
- docs/issues/: ISS-0001 is closed; ISS-0002 (this one) and ISS-0003 are open. ISS-0001 is in the same file and the same bar item (Q10). But its root cause was unguarded reads before the write phase, fixed with readTextFile. Its LOW rating rested on "команда падает до записи". Its fix holds: its 4 tests in cli.test.js:163-205 pass on the current code (my run below). ISS-0001 never touched the write loop. The root cause differs, so this is not a recurrence, and WF-03's "at least MAJOR on recurrence" does not apply.
- grep of sai/ (*.md, *.json, *.yaml; words частичн, атомар, atomic, partial, half-appl, наполовину, EISDIR, rename): no partial-write record before the ISS-0001 run. AP-006 (VERDICT-EXECUTOR stopped mid-way) wrote nothing: handoffs/WF06-20260925-01/step-05-verdict-executor.json says "STATE.md untouched". So it is not an earlier occurrence.
- [образец]/docs/anti-patterns.md (read-only grep for atomic, partial write, half-applied, rename, temp file): nothing on non-atomic multi-file writes.

SETUP (scratch only), W = <вне проекта>/iss0002-fixer
- Copies are made per case the way REVIEWER made them: rsync -a --exclude tools/node_modules --exclude .git <папка Sai>/ W/cases/<case>/sai.
- The CLI under test is the copy's own tools/src. Before each case, its manifest is checked against my baseline of live tools/src.
- Command: node <copy>/tools/src/cli.js apply-verdict <copy>/runs/WF06-20260926-01 --root <copy>.
- Before and after each run, W/strict_tree.py lists every entry: folders, files and symlinks, with type, mode, size, sha256 and mtime. A second variant leaves out mtime.
- To make STATE.md need a rewrite, one stale line goes after '### Рекомендация агентов (WF-06)' inside the existing block. Markers and the owner's section are untouched (15639 -> 15702 B).
- Harness: W/repro.sh, W/strict_tree.py, W/fixture-repro.mjs, W/mockprobe.test.mjs. Outputs: W/cases/<case>/{out,err}.txt and {before,after}.{strict,struct}.

CONTROLS
- C0a, no stale line: exit 0 'applied recommend'. Only apply-report.json changes (b80e6faf -> 5d806141). The real report records STATE.md as fbffcc3e..., but STATE.md has been e5ef7412... since later DOC-UPDATER edits. So on a fresh copy the report always needs a rewrite. This follows from the whole-file hash and is not a defect.
- C0b, stale line: exit 0 'applied recommend'. STATE.md goes 77be9843... (15702 B) -> e5ef7412... (15639 B), byte-identical to the real file. proposed-actions.json is byte-identical to the real one. Second run: 'unchanged', exit 0. So the listing catches writes.

M1 - A LATER TARGET FAILS AFTER STATE.md WAS WRITTEN. In every case below: exit 1, empty stdout, a Node trace with 8 '    at ' lines, and STATE.md already rewritten (77be9843... -> e5ef7412...).
- C1: proposed-actions.json is an empty folder. 'Error: EISDIR: illegal operation on a directory, read' at apply.js:103:34 (the compare-read). C1b, the same with a non-empty folder: same result.
- C2: apply-report.json is a folder, proposed-actions.json removed first. EISDIR at :103. STATE.md rewritten AND proposed-actions.json created (4504 B, 8075c20f...). C2b, with proposed-actions.json present: EISDIR, STATE.md rewritten.
- C3: run folder 555, outputs removed. "EACCES: permission denied, open '.../proposed-actions.json'" at apply.js:105:8.
- C4: apply-report.json 444. EACCES open at :105:8. C4b: proposed-actions.json 444 with one byte appended, so it must change. EACCES at :105:8.
- New variants, not in the issue:
  - C5: proposed-actions.json 000, content unchanged. EACCES at the compare-read, :103:34. C5b, apply-report.json 000: same.
  - C9a: apply-report.json is a dangling symlink into a missing folder. 'ENOENT ... open' at :105:8.
- Fixture runs (tools/test/helpers.js validRun, TMPDIR=W/tmp):
  - E1: escalate mode, first apply, apply-report.json is a folder. EISDIR at :103:34; STATE.md already has the escalation block.
  - E2: escalate mode, run folder 555. EACCES at :105:8; same.
  - F1: recommend, first apply (no block, outputs absent: the normal VERDICT-EXECUTOR path), proposed-actions.json is a folder. EISDIR; the block is already inserted.
  - F2: the same with apply-report.json as a folder. Block inserted AND proposed-actions.json added, then EISDIR.
  - F3: after F2, remove the folder and re-run: 'applied recommend', then 'unchanged'. M1 converges once the obstacle is gone.
- In-process: mock.method(fs, 'writeFileSync') throwing ENOSPC for apply-report.json. applyVerdict throws; STATE.md is already changed and proposed-actions.json created (W/mockprobe.test.mjs, pass).
- Code path of the trace: applyVerdict (apply.js:103 or :105) <- cli.js:129 <- main (cli.js:176). The catch in main (cli.js:177-183) handles only UsageError and rethrows everything else.

M2 - AN IN-PLACE WRITE FAILS PART-WAY (not in the issue; it hits the first target too)
- C8, run as bash -c 'ulimit -f 8; exec node ... apply-verdict ...'. EFBIG stands in for a mid-write ENOSPC, EDQUOT or EIO. Node ignores SIGXFSZ, so the error is an ordinary exception.
  - Result: exit 1, 'EFBIG: file too large, write' at :105. STATE.md 15702 -> 8192 B. The owner's section survives, but the end marker and '### Что делать дальше — по порядку' are gone.
  - Re-run without the limit: 'E_STATE_MARKERS STATE.md: block markers must appear exactly once each, start before end', exit 1. It does not converge.
- C8 with ulimit -f 4: STATE.md -> 4096 B. The owner's section (bytes 6082-6909 of the real file) is gone. Re-run: 'E_STATE_ANCHOR STATE.md: line not found: ### Что делать дальше — по порядку', exit 1.
- Real ENOSPC on an HFS+ 8 MB image mounted in the scratchpad (hdiutil).
  - Setup: a copy of sai/ with the wf06 block removed. This is the first apply: STATE.md must grow from 7823 B to 15639 B. The volume was filled with dd.
  - Result: exit 1, 'ENOSPC: no space left on device, write' at :105:8. STATE.md is left at 0 bytes, owner's section included.
  - After freeing space, re-run: E_STATE_ANCHOR, exit 1. STATE.md stays at 0 B.
- Real ENOSPC on APFS images (the macOS default), tried twice: a full volume, and a full volume with a 4 KiB gap.
  - Result: exit 1, "ENOSPC ... open '.../STATE.md'" at :105. APFS failed at open, before truncation. STATE.md was intact (7823 B), and the re-run gave 'applied recommend'.
  - So whether a full disk truncates STATE.md depends on the filesystem. The code has no protection of its own.
- sai/ is not tracked by git: git -C <общая папка> status --porcelain -- sai -> '?? sai/'. A truncated STATE.md has no VCS copy to restore from.

FACTS THE DESIGN NEEDS (my probes, this Mac)
- C3b: run folder 555 with the outputs present. Exit 0 'applied recommend': an in-place rewrite of an existing file needs no folder write permission.
- C7: project root 555. Exit 0; STATE.md is rewritten in place.
- C6: STATE.md 444 that must change. EACCES at :105 on the FIRST write, and nothing is written, not even an mtime (ISS-0003 case a). This is safe today only because STATE.md is written first.
- C9b: apply-report.json is a symlink to a file outside <root>. Exit 0. The report is written to the outside file, and the listing of <root> shows only STATE.md as changed.
- Rename probe on the scratch volume, umask 022:
  - renaming a file over an existing folder, empty or not: EISDIR;
  - renaming over a 444 file in a writable folder: succeeds, and the result has mode 644;
  - writeFileSync over a 0600 file keeps 0600;
  - creating a file in a 555 folder: EACCES, while an in-place write of an existing file there succeeds;
  - writeFileSync on a symlink writes through to its target; renaming over a symlink replaces the link.

ROOT CAUSE
- Code: apply.js:100-107 loops over [STATE.md, proposed-actions.json (recommend only), apply-report.json]. For each target it calls fs.existsSync plus fs.readFileSync (the compare-read, :103), then fs.writeFileSync (:105).
  - writeFileSync on an existing file opens it with truncation and writes in place.
  - The first target is STATE.md, the file that holds the owner's section.
  - Nothing is staged, pre-checked, ordered for consistency, rolled back, or turned into a §6 line. Any fs error on target k leaves the CLI as a trace. Targets 1..k-1 stay written (M1), and target k may be left truncated (M2).
  - The comment at apply.js:16 ('Every check runs before the first write; any issue means nothing is written') holds only for the checks.
- Design: §5 promises 'Сначала вся проверка, потом все записи' and no write on error. But item 5 ('Записать только файлы, содержимое которых отличается') has no failure model for the writes, and §6 has no code for a failed write. So the rule is kept for validation errors and silently broken for I/O errors of the write phase. §4.1 (prepare-run, 'ничего не создаётся') has the same gap; see SIBLINGS.
- Consequences for the fix:
  - The issue names only M1 ('на втором или третьем файле').
  - M2 happens under any write order, so writing STATE.md last does not fix it on its own.
  - A pre-check ('absent or a regular file', writable) cannot catch ENOSPC, EFBIG or EIO.
  - A try/catch that only turns the exception into an error line removes the trace but keeps both M1 and M2. That is a symptom fix (Q6).

WHY THE EXISTING TESTS DID NOT CATCH IT
(a) REQ-002 AC6/AC7 and design §9 tie 'nothing is written' only to pre-write checks (apply.reject.test.js, apply.state.test.js). No criterion, design row or test covers a failure of the write phase itself, and §6 has no code a test could expect.
(b) No test puts an obstacle on a write target or injects an fs failure. The only folder or chmod setups in tools/test are on read-phase inputs (cli.test.js:163-205, validate.run.test.js:109-121, prepare.test.js:58), and nothing mocks fs. On the scratch copy, node --test test/apply.*.test.js test/cli.test.js gives tests 25, pass 25, fail 0.
(c) tree() (helpers.js:350, through util.js listFiles :68-81, which keeps only entry.isFile()) is blind to several changes (W/fixture-repro.mjs T1-T5): an added empty or nested folder, a mode change from 644 to 444, and a symlink. It also throws EACCES on a mode-000 file. So a fix that left a folder or a symlink behind, or changed a mode, would still pass today's assertions (REVIEWER O2).

SEVERITY - FOR ORCH
MEDIUM rests on two reasons: 'it needs a deliberate folder or permission change' and 'a re-run converges'. Both hold for M1. For M2 on HFS+ (ENOSPC), neither holds: no deliberate setup is needed, STATE.md was emptied, the re-run is refused, and there is no git copy. On APFS my full-disk attempts failed safely at open, and the file-size limit (EFBIG) is a deliberate setting. I recommend that ORCH re-rate M2 (HIGH, or split it into its own issue). The issue text also needs correcting: the first file can fail as well, and truncation is possible. This is not a recurrence, so WF-03 does not force MAJOR.

WHAT THE FIX DESIGN MUST DECIDE (for CODE-DESIGNER; I do not design it)
D1 - The guarantee, written as testable §5 text.
  - For each handled failure: the exit code, the §6 line(s), no trace, empty stdout, and a strict listing of <root> that is identical before and after (folders, symlinks, types, file bytes, modes).
  - Whether folder mtimes are excluded: a temp file that is created and then removed changes its folder's mtime.
  - What is promised if the process is killed or loses power between steps, e.g. 'each target holds its old or its new bytes, never a truncated mix'.
D2 - The write strategy. From the evidence:
  - No in-place write of an existing target (M2).
  - All failure-prone work happens before the first visible change: the compare-reads (C1, C2 and C5 fail at :103), the type and permission checks, and writing the new bytes in full to a temp file beside each target (a rename is atomic only within one folder and filesystem).
  - The commit renames are not atomic as a set. Choose their order and the commit point. Note that STATE.md's block names proposed-actions.json (apply.js:138), and apply-report.json records the sha256 of STATE.md and of proposed-actions.json (apply.js:89-98).
  - Say what happens if rename k fails after renames 1..k-1: roll back from the old bytes already read at :103, or print a distinct message?
  - Pre-check what makes a rename fail predictably, such as a folder target (EISDIR).
  - Keep 'skip unchanged targets; print unchanged' (§5 item 5).
D3 - Behaviour that a rename-based strategy changes. Each needs an explicit rule and a test.
  - A 444 target in a writable folder: today EACCES (C4, C6); a rename would silently replace it and reset its mode to 644. Honour the mode, or replace the file?
  - Mode and inode: kept today; after a rename, the file has the temp's mode. Preserve them?
  - A read-only folder with writable existing targets: exit 0 today (C3b, C7); staging a temp there fails. Accept the new failure?
  - Symlinked targets are followed today. A dangling link gives ENOENT after STATE.md was written (C9a); a link out of <root> is written outside the project with exit 0 (C9b). A rename would replace the link. Reject with the §6 code, replace, or follow? (Q11: design §10 keeps the run folder inside runs/.)
D4 - Temp files.
  - Placed in the target's own folder and created exclusively.
  - The name must not match validate's run-folder scans: validate.js:142-150 matches '^(assessment|crossreview|response)-(.+)\.json$' and gives E_LENS; :603-625 matches verdict-N and verdict-review-N. The name must also stay clear of the snapshot-diff checks (REQ-004 AC4, REQ-006).
  - Removed on every failure path, including when the cleanup itself fails.
  - Decide what to do with a stale temp left by a killed run, and whether fsync and power-loss durability are in scope.
D5 - The §6 code for a failed write. ISS-0003 reuses it for its write cases a, b, e and g1.
  - Its name, and its exit code: 1 like the other violations, or a new one? §6 defines only 0, 1 and 2.
  - The <файл> field: relative to <root> for apply. The snapshot out-file (cli.js:145) may be outside <root>, and a mistyped out-file folder (g1) might instead be E_USAGE with code 2.
  - The message should state the OS code (EISDIR, EACCES, ENOENT, ENOSPC, EFBIG, EROFS) and that nothing was changed. If D2 allows a failure after the commit point, it must say exactly what changed.
  - Whether a target that cannot be read for the comparison (C5) uses the same code.
  - Whether every failing target is reported, or only the first.
  - How the error leaves applyVerdict without a catch-all in main (cli.js:177-183). A catch-all would also hide programming errors; REVIEWER credited ISS-0001 for avoiding one.
D6 - Scope with the sibling paths (AP-014): see SIBLINGS. ORCH decides.
D7 - Paperwork, in the same work (Q1, Q5, Q14): §5 item 5 (and §4.1 if prepare-run is included), a new row in §6, and the §9 mapping. REQ-002 has no acceptance criterion for write failures; AC6/AC7 cover only pre-write checks. ORCH decides whether REQ-ANALYST adds one so that the new tests map to a criterion.

TEST MATRIX (for TEST-DESIGNER; fail-first on context.pre_fix_copy)
Targets: S = STATE.md; P = runs/<RUN-ID>/proposed-actions.json (recommend mode only); R = runs/<RUN-ID>/apply-report.json.
States:
- recommend, first apply: no block, outputs absent (F1, F2).
- recommend, re-apply: the block with a stale line, outputs present (the C cases).
- escalate, first apply: P must never appear (E1, E2).
Failure kinds:
- K1, empty folder: P (C1, F1); R (C2, C2b, F2, E1). For S this is E_STATE_ANCHOR at the read today (ISS-0001); keep it as a regression row.
- K2, non-empty folder: P (C1b), R. For S, the same as K1.
- K3, read-only file (444) whose content must change: S (C6), P (C4b), R (C4).
- K4, existing but unreadable (000): P (C5), R (C5b). For S, readTextFile catches it today (E_STATE_ANCHOR).
- K5, read-only containing folder (555): the run folder with outputs absent (C3, E2); the run folder with outputs present (C3b, exit 0 today); the root (C7, exit 0 today). The expected result follows D3.
- K6, write fails part-way (ENOSPC, EFBIG, EIO), for each target. Inject the failure, e.g. a spawned CLI under a file-size limit (C8; bash ulimit, POSIX only) or node:test mock.method on the fs default export (verified to reach the fs calls in apply.js). Assert that no target is truncated.
- K7, a failure at the commit step, e.g. the k-th rename throws (injection only). Assert the D2 rule.
- K8, symlinked target: dangling (C9a), or pointing out of <root> (C9b, with the outside file included in the listing).
Assertions for every row:
- the exit code;
- stderr is exactly the §6 line(s), anchored, naming the right target;
- no '^\s+at ' line;
- stdout is empty;
- the strict listing of <root> is equal before and after, including folders, symlinks, types and modes; a leftover temp file shows up here;
- after the obstacle is removed, 'applied <mode>' and then 'unchanged', with bytes equal to a clean apply;
- one control per fixture without the obstacle, proving that the listing sees the writes.
Notes for the test spec:
- Chmod rows need a non-root user (the existing idiom, cli.test.js:173).
- tree() cannot hash a 000 file (T5). Take the listing before chmod and after the mode is restored, as cli.test.js:174-185 does, or let the new listing skip reading unreadable files.
- tree() sees regular files only, so extend it or add a listing that includes folders, types and modes. D1 decides how folder mtimes are handled.
- For each row, state whether it fails before the fix, and on which assertion. On the pre-fix copy, the M1 rows, C6, C8 and C9a fail: there is a trace, a changed STATE.md, or a truncated STATE.md. A row whose pre-fix result already matches the chosen behaviour (e.g. C3b or C7, if exit 0 is kept) locks behaviour in; it is not fail-first proof.

- prepare-run, prepare.js:133-138. Reproduced:

Q13 PROPOSAL (candidate AP-015, for DOC-UPDATER through ORCH)

It states a write strategy and a commit point, and gives an error code and a fault-injection test for each target. CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR checks that the test matrix has rows for write failures.
